sections.h2: What towns and landmarks make up Greene County?
sections.html:
Greene County occupies Georgia's east central Lake country, with Greensboro serving as seat and as its largest community. Lawmakers formed it on February 3, 1786 out of Washington County land, and it carries the name of Nathanael Greene, a major general of the Revolution (Wikipedia).

Of 406 square miles in total, 387 are land and 19, or 4.6%, are water. Streams drain three ways: the Oconee River across the west, the Little River flowing toward the Savannah in the north, and the Ogeechee system in the south. Part of Oconee National Forest reaches into the county, and the extinct river town of Scull Shoals recalls the county's earlier years. Interstate 20 runs through, with US 278 and State Routes 12, 15, 44 and 77 as other main roads.

The incorporated places are Greensboro, Union Point, White Plains, Woodville and the town of Siloam, and Bairdstown is an unincorporated community. Oglethorpe, Taliaferro, Hancock, Putnam, Morgan and Oconee counties ring it. Local families can choose among the Greene County School Board, Lake Oconee Academy and Nathanael Greene Academy. A house on the lake and a house in town receive their bills from the same tax commissioner.

sections.h2: How have Greene County's population and housing changed?
sections.html:
The 2020 count found 18,915 residents, and the July 2025 estimate of 21,367 is 13.0% higher. People aged 65 and up are 33.5% of the total, about one in three, which is why the senior exemptions further down reach many local owners. Looking back, Wikipedia's table lists 5,405 people in 1790 and 17,547 in 1880, and QuickFacts shows 15,994 in 2010. Wikipedia links recent growth to people moving to Reynolds Lake Oconee.

sections.h2: Which Greene County office takes which tax question?
sections.html:
Both offices share one address on Silver Drive in Greensboro, and three other bodies shape the bill. The county commissioners and the school board each levy a rate to fund their own budgets, and a Board of Equalization named by the grand jury hears disputes over the assessors' values. The commissioner handles bills and collections for land and buildings, business property, mobile homes, vehicles, timber and utilities, and also issues vehicle tags as the state's agent. Values, returns and exemption approvals sit with the tax assessors.

  • Tax Commissioner: Suite 101 at 1034 Silver Drive, Greensboro, GA 30642, phone 706-453-3358, lobby hours run Monday to Friday, from eight until a quarter to five.
  • Tax Assessors: Suite 102 in the same building, phone 706-453-3355, for values, appeals and homestead filings.
  • Online: the county website has a homestead application page and a separate page on the yearly digest and assessments.

Hours and forms appear on the commissioner's page and the assessors' appeal page.

sections.h2: When does Greene County expect payment?
sections.html:
The county sets December 1 as its payment date and pushes it to the next working day if the 1st is a Saturday, Sunday or holiday. Per the commissioner's page, land whose tax goes unpaid may be levied on and later sold.

Other dates follow a set pattern. A return lists what you held on January 1 and can be filed through April 1. Land and buildings carry forward at their earlier value, whereas business and other personal property need a new return every year. Under the state's county facts sheet, a mobile home must be returned by April 1 and its location permit renewed between January 1 and April 1. Assessment notices tend to go out around May, with millage rates set later.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Greene County assessment?
sections.html:
Owners get 45 days from the day the notice was mailed. You may argue taxability, value, uniformity or a refused exemption, using the state's PT-311A form sent to the Board of Tax Assessors. That first filing also has to say which route you are taking.

  • Equalization route: the assessors look at it first and may issue a corrected notice, which you can contest within 30 days; an appeal they leave alone is heard by the Board of Equalization, and Superior Court is the final stop.
  • Hearing officer: a certified appraiser can take value disputes, but only on real property that is not a homestead and is valued at $1,000,000 or above.
  • Arbitration: attach a current certified appraisal. When the assessors turn it down, the case moves to the clerk of Superior Court, a hearing follows inside 30 days, and the arbitrator's ruling is final.

The county page walks through each route and points to the state revenue department for forms.

sections.h2: Which homestead exemptions does Greene County use?
sections.html:
For a given year you must own the home and live in it on January 1, then file by April 1; anything later waits for the next year. Once approved, the exemption carries on yearly until ownership, residence or exemption type changes. The county's chart lists these deductions from assessed value:

  • S1, the state default: $2,000, applied to county and school taxes.
  • L1, age 65 and over: $10,000, described as $2,000 state plus $8,000 local.
  • S3, ages 62 to 64, net income capped at $10,000: $2,000 on county taxes and $10,000 on school taxes.
  • L4, age 65 and over, net income capped at $10,000: $12,000 on county taxes and $18,000 on school taxes.
  • S5 and L5, a 100% disabled veteran or unremarried surviving spouse: $100,896, a 2021 state figure that changes annually and needs proof.

A trailing F on a code, as in S1F, flags the homestead freeze, an exemption equal to any rise in assessed value since the day the exemption was approved. As the county describes it, the freeze covers the house and land up to five acres, and it excludes pools, barns, detached garages and shops (county homestead page). The county also describes a deferral program that lets owners aged 62 and older delay, though not cancel, their tax if household income reaches no more than $15,000, and farmland that qualifies is assessed at 30%.

sections.h2: What should a Greene County seller do about tax before closing?
sections.html:
According to the state revenue department, whoever holds title on January 1 stays liable for the whole year, even when the house sells the next day, and there is no refund for a partial year. Contracts usually split the bill, so the number to find is the exact balance on the parcel.

Get a written statement from the commissioner's office showing tax owed now and for earlier years. If the sale falls close to December 1, ask which amount the closing agent should send. Keep the assessment notice and any appeal paperwork in the file, since a pending appeal can alter the final bill. Tell the assessors in writing when you move out, so your homestead code comes off the property and the next owner can apply in their name.

faqs.q: Which day does Greene County collect property tax?
faqs.a: December 1, moving to the next business day if that is a weekend or holiday. A parcel with unpaid tax can be levied on and in time sold, the commissioner's page says.

faqs.q: How much time do I have to dispute a Greene County value?
faqs.a: Forty-five days from the mailing date on your assessment notice. The Board of Tax Assessors needs a written appeal naming your route, which can be equalization, a hearing officer or arbitration.

faqs.q: By what date must I file Greene County homestead paperwork?
faqs.a: April 1 for the present tax year. The home must have been yours and your residence on January 1, and later applications count for the year after.

faqs.q: What does the code S1F mean on a Greene County notice?
faqs.a: The F marks the homestead freeze, an exemption equal to any rise in assessed value above the level on the day your homestead was approved. It applies to the house and land up to five acres, with pools, barns, detached garages and shops left out, according to the county.

faqs.q: Which Greene County office do I phone about a bill or a value?
faqs.a: The tax commissioner, at 706-453-3358, takes bills and payments, and the tax assessors, at 706-453-3355, take values, appeals and exemptions. Both work from 1034 Silver Drive in Greensboro.
